transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately and what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just feel like I don't deserve the trust people put in me. I'm a physician, and lately, I just keep replaying these small clinical imperfections in my head. It's like... like they prove I'm a dangerous doctor or something. It's just really weighing on me.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or experiencing feelings of worthlessness most days lately?

Yes, I have. Um... definitely the worthlessness. I just feel really down most days lately. It's hard to shake the feeling that I'm doing harm or failing my patients, so... yeah, I guess hopeless fits, too. I just feel very low.
Have you ever had an episode like this before, where you felt down and hopeless for a period of time?

No, I haven't. I mean... obviously medical school and residency were stressful, and I've had hard days before, but I've never felt this down or hopeless for an extended period of time. This is... this is really the first time it's been like this.

Are these feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness limited to your work as a physician, or do they also affect other areas of your life, like your personal relationships or activities you usually enjoy?

It definitely affects other areas of my life, yeah. I used to really enjoy planning things outside of work... like weekend hikes, taking sunrise photos, or cooking big Indonesian dinners for my friends. But for months now, I just haven't had any interest in doing any of that. It's gotten to the point where those things just feel like heavy obligations, and I... I just can't make myself care about them anymore.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before where you felt down, hopeless, or had thoughts of worthlessness that lasted for several weeks or more?
I think... didn't you just ask me that? But no, like I said, I've never had a period like this before. This is the first time it's lasted this long and felt this bad.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or have you noticed a lack of energy lately, even after getting enough rest?

I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I feel drained from just how heavy everything feels right now, but it's not like I'm physically exhausted or lacking energy in a way that stands out, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like cooking or hiking, no longer give you any pleasure or satisfaction?

I... I feel like I just answered that a minute ago. But yeah, like I said, I don't get any enjoyment out of them anymore. Cooking, hiking, photography... none of it brings me any pleasure now. It just feels like a chore.
Have you felt down or in a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at any point during this current period?

I... wait, I feel like we're going in circles here. Didn't you just ask me about feeling down? But, uh, yeah. Like I mentioned before, I've been feeling really low and down most of the day, every day, for weeks now. It's just a constant heavy feeling.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty normal, I think. I haven't lost or gained any weight that I've noticed, so... yeah, I'm eating about the same as usual.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless or fidgety, like you can't sit still?

Yeah, definitely the moving slowly part. At work, I've noticed I just move so slowly between rooms... and then I'll sit there staring at the EHR for a while before I actually click anything. It's gotten to the point where the nurses have started gently asking me if I'm okay. So, yeah, I'm definitely a lot slower than usual.
Have you ever felt so restless that you couldn't sit still or found yourself pacing around, or have these slowing-down feelings been the main issue for you?

No, not restless at all. It's really just the slowing down, like I was just saying. That's definitely the main issue for me. I just... I move so slowly between rooms at work, and I'll just sit there staring at the EHR before I actually click anything. It's noticeable enough that the nurses keep gently asking if I'm alright. So, yeah, just the slowing down, no pacing or anything like that.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or found yourself thinking that life isn't worth living anymore?

Well... I don't have a plan to kill myself or anything like that. But I do catch myself thinking that it might be better if I just didn't wake up. It usually hits me the hardest after a day when I'm convinced I've let my patients down.
Can you clarify again whether you have ever experienced a period of feeling this down, hopeless, or struggling with worthlessness before in your life, even if it was shorter or not as intense?
No, I haven't. This is the first time I've ever felt like this. I've never had a period where I felt this down or hopeless before.

Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, elated, or extremely confident, or had more energy than usual to the point where others might have noticed a change in your behavior?

No, never. I haven't ever had a period where I felt unusually high or... or had extreme energy like that. I've always just been pretty even-keeled, at least until recently when everything just slowed down. So, no, nothing like what you're describing.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt so down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, even before this current time?

Like I mentioned just a minute ago, no. I've never had a time where I felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks before this current stretch. This is really the first time I've ever dealt with anything like this.

Can you recall if your current feelings of hopelessness and worthlessness have been continuous since they started, or if there have been any noticeable breaks where you felt like your usual self, even briefly?

It's been pretty continuous, honestly. I haven't really noticed any breaks... or any days where I felt like my old self again, even for a little bit. It's just been a constant weight since it all started.

So far, we've talked about several symptoms you've been experiencing—feeling down, loss of interest in activities, feeling worthless, moving more slowly, and thoughts that life isn't worth living. In total, how many of these kinds of symptoms have you experienced during this current period?

I haven't really counted them up, to be honest. I mean, I've definitely been experiencing the ones you just listed—the feeling down, losing interest, feeling worthless, moving slower, and... those thoughts. But I don't have a specific number for you. I haven't been keeping a tally or anything, it all just kind of blends together into this one heavy feeling right now.
